known_facts_book1: The good Sorceress who rules the Quadlings of the red South country and is the most skilled in magic in all Oz.
Now owns the Golden Cap that commands the Winged Monkeys (recalled as past history by the Scarecrow).
Reveals to the Scarecrow that the throne rightfully belongs to Pastoria's heir, and reads her book of the Wizard's actions to deduce Mombi hid the child Ozma.
Marches her trained girl army, armed with swords and spears, on the Emerald City to seize Mombi.
Sees through Mombi's decoys and disguises: exposes Jellia disguised as Mombi, and detects the rose, shadow, ant, and Griffin transformations.
Captures Mombi with a golden thread and forces the truth from her with a white pearl that turns black at a lie.
Makes Mombi confess and undo the enchantment, restoring Ozma, then installs Ozma as Queen and advises her.

known_relations_book1.Mombi: Her adversary, whom she pursues, out-magics, captures, and strips of magical power.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Petitions her for help; she guides him to the true heir Ozma.
known_relations_book1.Tip: Takes a great liking to the boy; reveals and restores his identity as Princess Ozma and becomes her adviser.
known_relations_book1.Nick Chopper: The Tin Woodman, whom she knows and likes; he unknowingly carries Mombi to her as a rose.

adaptation_or_confusion: Glinda the Good Witch of the North
Glinda gives Dorothy the ruby slippers
Glinda arrives in a floating bubble

known_facts_book1: A green-clad maid of the Emerald City palace, born in the northern Gillikin country, summoned to interpret between the Scarecrow and Jack.
Mischievously mistranslates, telling Jack the Scarecrow's brains have come loose and telling the Scarecrow that Jack insulted him.
Reveals that only one language is spoken in all Oz, so no interpreter was ever needed.
Is magically disguised as Mombi and handed to Glinda as a decoy, then breaks down weeping under questioning.
Is restored to her true shape by Glinda, confesses Mombi's trick, and is granted the Sorceress's protection.

known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: His palace servant and 'interpreter,' whom she teases with false translations.
known_relations_book1.Mombi: Forces her to take Mombi's form as a decoy and threatens her with death if she confesses.
known_relations_book1.Jack Pumpkinhead: The visitor she interprets (and mistranslates) for.

not_in_this_book: Jellia Jamb is the rightful heir Ozma

known_facts_book1: The Emerald City's lone soldier and entire Royal Army; wears a green uniform and green whiskers to his knees and carries a green gun that is never loaded.
Escorts Jack to the Scarecrow and serves as the city's only guard.
Flees when Jinjur's girls attack, because his gun is unloaded and he is afraid of women.
Locks the Saw-Horse in the treasury as a 'jewel,' then ties the escaping party together and is left behind.
Offers to cut off his lovely green whiskers to disguise himself.

known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: His sovereign, whom he serves as the whole Royal Army of Oz.
known_relations_book1.Guardian of the Gates: Fellow palace functionary who rings for him to handle newcomers.
known_relations_book1.Jinjur: Routs his one-man army without a fight.

known_facts_book1: The fat, green-clad, green-spectacled keeper of the Emerald City gates, who fits green spectacles on all who enter to guard against the glare.
Meets Jack and the Saw-Horse and, puzzled, sends them on to the Scarecrow.
Refuses Jinjur's demand to surrender ('It's against the law!'), then is mobbed with knitting-needles and has his keys taken.
A new Guardian, a fussy fat woman appointed by Jinjur, is later bowled over by the escaping Saw-Horse.

known_relations_book1.Jinjur: Demands his surrender and seizes his keys when he refuses.
known_relations_book1.Soldier with the Green Whiskers: Rings for the Soldier to deal with strange arrivals.
known_relations_book1.Jack Pumpkinhead: Admits him to the city and puzzles over him.

not_in_this_book: the Guardian of the Gates admits Dorothy
the Guardian refuses to let the party leave
